summary: Pentti Aalto worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics from 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen, where he later lectured (1982–1989), before serving as professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kværne is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1963–1973) under Nils Simonsson. His career includes lecturing at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and working as an editorial consultant at Oslo (1975–2007).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Rau from around 1965 to 1970. He held a post at the University of Marburg.

Perry Link is a Sinologist and linguist who earned his B.A. from Harvard University (~1962–1966). He taught at Princeton (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside, where he was appointed Chancellorial Chair Professor around 2008.

Perry Schmidt-Leukel works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Munich (~1977–1996), he held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson is a philosopher and Indologist. He completed his studies at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1995–2000), subsequently holding academic posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).
Peter Alan Roberts specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and under doctoral supervisor Michael Aris.

Peter C. Bisschop is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004 under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit Studies at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010).

Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Yale University and with teachers Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim and Seungsahn Haengwon. He coordinated the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.
Peter Fenner specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Advised by Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, he held an academic post at Deakin University.

Indologist Peter Gaeffke earned his PhD from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1948–1952) and also studied at Regensburg and DIAS. He served as a professor at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at the London School of Economics by 1990. He held an adjunct post at Adams State University, attested in 2007.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2000–2015).
Peter Haskel specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he was taught by Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson completed his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1956–1961), where he also taught (~1960–1965). He later taught at Vassar College, the University of Washington, Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and the Australian National University (PhD attested 2010), supervised by John Powers alongside several traditional teachers.
Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University from 1975 to 1978 and held a post at SOAS University of London from around 2002 to 2018.
